arguments.description: Run fact_inventory model and verify row uniqueness

text:
`fact_inventory` now has one row per `inventory_id`: 102 rows, 102 distinct ids, after a successful `dbt run --select fact_inventory`.

The cause was 52 duplicated rows in `stg_inventory_transactions`. The 154 source rows contain only 102 distinct ids, and the duplicates were exact copies of each other.

The change is in `models/warehouse/fact_inventory.sql`: I added a `QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY inventory_id ORDER BY transaction_modified_date DESC NULLS LAST, transaction_created_date DESC) = 1` clause. I chose this over `SELECT DISTINCT` so the uniqueness holds even if a future load has rows for the same id that differ. Since the current duplicates are identical, the choice of row doesn't change the output.

I did not rerun `obt_product_inventory`, which reads from `fact_inventory`. It may have had inflated row counts from the duplicates, so it will change on its next run.

VERDICT: fixed
